hypothesis: H84-1/H84-3 (fused): blind, altered fault conduits produce a local RTP magnetic-amplitude MINIMUM (demagnetization from hydrothermal alteration) spatially conjugate with a local surface-conductivity HIGH (clay-cap/argillic alteration), and/or a basement-high (shallow depth_to_base_surf) that is anomalously conductive at surface (a fault-controlled conduit cross-cutting a horst). Both are pure functions of 4 official bands (rtp, cond_surf, tmi_hg, depth_to_base_surf); neither uses labels.tif as a model input.
mechanism: Hydrothermal fluid circulation along a fault destroys primary magnetite (demagnetization) and deposits clay/argillic alteration minerals that raise near-surface electrical conductivity; the alteration halo can be broad and blind (no surface rupture) when the fault does not reach the surface expression mapped by USGS/INGENIOUS, which is exactly the catalogue-gap the competition is scoring for.
named_non_fault_mimic: Thick, undeformed sedimentary basin-fill produces the SAME joint signature (low magnetization, high near-surface conductivity from clay/groundwater) with NO fault control whatsoever. A Sato ridge/vesselness filter was used specifically to try to prefer elongated, fault-aligned corridors over this basin-fill's broad, equant lows -- diagnostics below show this guard was insufficient.

evidence_sources.claim: Hydrothermal demagnetization / magnetic-low association with geothermal fault conduits is a real, reproducible phenomenon in Basin-and-Range and caldera settings
Competition metric formula (DTI, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, R=300m triangular kernel)

holdout_dti.evaluator_version: gems84.metric v1 (crop-exact finite-kernel), gems84.holdout v1 (6x6 spatially-checkerboarded blocks, 6 folds, 3px/300m buffer, whole-segment withholding)
holdout_dti.note: Computed against the PUBLIC USGS/INGENIOUS fault catalogue (labels.tif), which is NOT the private expert-labelled test set the real competition scores against. This is the only ground truth available in any sandbox in this lineage.
holdout_dti.verdict_detail: At every emission budget tested (15,000 to 1,000,000 px, i.e. 0.3%-19.4% of the 5,164,300-px footprint), a spatially-UNIFORM-random field outperforms the fused H84 field by 2.8x-4.3x. This gap is NOT explained by the leakage canary (all AUCs 0.507-0.517, i.e. barely above the 0.500 chance line and nowhere near the 0.90 leakage threshold) -- it is explained by a spatial-coverage mechanism quantified directly: 8.16% of the entire footprint lies within the 300 m kernel radius of SOME mapped fault (the catalogue is geographically pervasive across this Basin-and-Range terrain), so ANY spatially-uniform emission earns substantial credit purely from ubiquity, while the H84 field concentrates its highest-confidence mass in specific sub-basins whose geometry does not coincide with where the mapped range-front fault network actually runs -- i.e. the named non-fault mimic (basin-fill lows) dominates the field's extreme tail despite the Sato ridge-filter guard.

correlation_vs_registry.note: This is a freshly-initialized repository (GEMSDOE84) with no prior submissions of its own to compare against. We cross-checked our implementation's uniform-random baseline (0.0498-0.0608 depending on exact holdout construction) against the independently-computed uniform-random baseline reported in a sibling repository's own knowledge base (buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32, commit c0c06ac8-era checkout, docs/research and knowledge/02_the_ceiling_and_the_instrument.md: 'uniform random (3 seeds) 0.0498') -- same order of magnitude, different holdout construction, which cross-validates that our metric/holdout implementation is not pathologically broken. We did NOT compute pixel-level rank correlation against every raster in every sibling repo (80+ repositories); that full audit is listed as a limitation below.
correlation_vs_registry.limitation: Full rank-correlation / 3px-overlap duplicate-lane check against all registry rasters was not completed given the 3-experiment/time budget; see 'Suggested next steps' in README.md.

nan_variant.note: NaN only OUTSIDE the scoring footprint, matching the spec's literal text; shipped as a SECONDARY file because of the user's own reported portal error ('Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]') on a NaN-outside file from a different pipeline -- see README Known Issues.
